name: Nurture 01 - Map the review
subject: A useful starting point for your review workflow
paragraphs: Thanks for your interest in Hierarchia. Start with one recurring deliverable, one reviewer and the three checks that most often send work back.
Reply with the type of submission your team reviews most often. We can use an anonymized example; no confidential files are needed.
The first conversation is a free, 20-minute workflow audit. A paid pilot is scoped separately if there is a good fit.

name: Nurture 02 - Find the baseline
subject: How many hours disappear into repeat reviews?
paragraphs: A practical baseline needs only three numbers: submissions each week, minutes per review and the percentage returned for another pass.
Measure a typical week before changing the process. The goal is to test whether a clearer checklist helps—not to assume an AI tool automatically saves time.
If you would like to compare notes, reply with those three numbers and the kind of work your team delivers.

name: Nurture 03 - Human decisions
subject: Which checks belong to AI—and which stay with a manager?
paragraphs: Missing sections and incomplete source details can be flagged for attention. Context, sensitive judgments and final acceptance should stay with your team.
Hierarchia combines standing rules and task-specific briefs in a role-aware submission workflow. AI output still needs evaluation against representative work.
Which recurring check would be most useful to make explicit for your team?

name: Nurture 04 - Pilot scope
subject: What a small Hierarchia pilot would test
paragraphs: A focused pilot starts with one team and no more than two repeatable workflows. We agree the baseline, reviewer responsibilities and acceptance criteria before it begins.
Over 30 days, compare review time, repeat submissions and reviewer agreement. Hosting, integrations, data handling, price and support are scoped together—not assumed.
Would it be useful to map a pilot around one of your existing workflows?

name: Nurture 05 - Close the loop
subject: Should we keep this on your list?
paragraphs: Is improving submission review a priority right now, something for later, or not relevant to your team?
Reply with whichever fits. If it is not a priority, we can close the loop. You can also unsubscribe below at any time.
